headline: Galápagos Atlas Opens Window Into Island Life—and Scientific Mysteries
meta_description: A new freely available atlas created by 87 scientists and conservationists profiles 68 species across the Galápagos Islands, revealing both what we know and wh…

body:
The Darwin Foundation has released a groundbreaking new atlas that profiles 68 species and species groups across the Galápagos Islands—from the iconic giant tortoises and Darwin finches to lesser-known creatures like carpenter bees and kelp. Created by a team of 87 authors, scientists, park rangers, and conservationists, the freely available atlas does something unusual: it highlights not just what researchers have discovered about each species, but also what remains unknown about their ecology, behavior, and conservation needs. This approach transforms the atlas from a reference book into an invitation. As Darwin Foundation executive director Rakan Zahawi explained, the atlas serves as a starting point for anyone captivated by the islands' mysteries, with each species entry providing citations and research leads to follow deeper into the subject.

The atlas also documents a pressing conservation challenge: the Galápagos now hosts around 1,500 introduced species, with just over 60 classified as invasive and disrupting native ecosystems. Rather than simply cataloging the problem, the resource aims to raise awareness about preventing further introductions—especially among tourists who may inadvertently transport species to the islands. The atlas includes primers on the natural history, human history, ecology, evolution, and geology of the archipelago, offering context that connects individual species to their larger environment.

Conservationists view the atlas as a vital tool. Island Conservation CEO Penny Becker noted that by combining current knowledge with clearly identified research gaps, the atlas can guide more effective conservation decisions. Editor-in-chief Gustavo Jiménez hopes future editions will expand the species covered and add Spanish-language versions, ensuring the resource reaches even broader audiences across the region.
quick_facts: 87 scientists, artists, and conservationists created the atlas
68 species and species groups profiled in the archipelago
1,500 introduced species now present in the Galápagos
Freely available online resource with citations for further research
Created by the Darwin Foundation to guide conservation action
